references.text: Samuel also defends his integrity before the people and claims that he has not taken anyone's donkey or oppressed anyone, just as Moses here defends himself before God.
God looked with favor on Abel's offering, but not on Cain's. Here Moses asks God not to look with favor on the rebels' offerings.
Moses shows similar anger and intercedes for the Lord, this time in connection with the golden calf.
Moses is described as very gentle, but here we see that even he could become very angry when falsely accused.
Paul defends his ministry in a similar way and claims that he has not coveted anyone's silver, gold, or clothing.
Paul defends himself against accusations and says that he has done no wrong to anyone, just as Moses does here.
Paul asks whether he or his fellow workers have taken advantage of the congregation, similar to Moses' defense of his integrity.
